\section[el diagnóstico]{el diagnóstico — the diagnosis}

\label{lesson:ES-C738-diagnostico}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the hip, then the Spanish for the rib.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el diagnóstico}
\textbf{el diagnóstico} — \textquotedblleft{}the diagnosis\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El médico ya tiene el diagnóstico.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The doctor has the diagnosis now.}
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{diagnóstico} is a learned word built on Greek \emph{diagnōstikós} \textquotedblleft{}able to distinguish\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{diagign\'{\={o}}skein} \textquotedblleft{}to tell apart\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{gign\'{\={o}}skein} \textquotedblleft{}to know\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el diagnóstico}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el diagnóstico}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el diagnóstico}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the hip, then the Spanish for the rib, then say \emph{el diagnóstico} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does el diagnóstico mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The diagnosis\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[el síntoma]{el síntoma — the symptom}

\label{lesson:ES-C738-sintoma}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the diagnosis, then the Spanish for to diagnose.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el síntoma}
\textbf{el síntoma} — \textquotedblleft{}the symptom\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
¿Qué síntomas tiene?
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{What symptoms do you have?}
\end{quote}

Masculine, though it ends in \emph{-a}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{síntoma} comes from Late Latin \emph{symptōma}, from Greek \emph{sýmptōma} \textquotedblleft{}a happening, a symptom\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[el tratamiento]{el tratamiento — the treatment}

\label{lesson:ES-C738-tratamiento}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to diagnose, then the Spanish for the symptom.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el tratamiento}
\textbf{el tratamiento} — \textquotedblleft{}the treatment\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El tratamiento dura dos semanas.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The treatment lasts two weeks.}
\end{quote}

Also a form of address: \emph{el tratamiento de usted}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tratamiento} is built on \emph{tratar} \textquotedblleft{}to treat\textquotedblright{}, which is usually traced to Latin \emph{tractāre} \textquotedblleft{}to handle\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\section[padecer]{padecer — to suffer from}

\label{lesson:ES-C738-padecer}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the symptom, then the Spanish for the treatment.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: padecer}
\textbf{padecer} — \textquotedblleft{}to suffer from\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Padece una enfermedad del corazón.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{She suffers from a heart condition.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Padecer de} + illness. More formal than \emph{sufrir}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{padecer} is inherited from a spoken Latin \emph{patīscere} (EtymDB), from \emph{patī} \textquotedblleft{}to suffer\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
